text: diseasenowcasting standalone R package Bayesian epidemic nowcasting using RTMB autodiff engine (CppAD + built-Laplace approximation). reimplements diseasenowcast2 Stan-based package Stan/cmdstanr dependency, matching public API: model(likelihood(), epidemic(), delay()). Core idea: reporting delay stochastic process modelled jointly epidemic. likelihood depends observed delays (reporting triangle), censoring handled cleanly. Laplace approximation marginalises latent epidemic coefficients; posterior draws sampled N(mode, H⁻¹) H joint Hessian. Default mode: joint-mode Laplace (use_random = FALSE) — cmdstanr $laplace(). 20–400× faster marginal (random=) Laplace. Two-stage cascade: Stage 1 fits delay (delay_only = TRUE); Stage 2 hard-fixes delay K imputed values pools draws. propagates delay uncertainty without sacrificing convergence.

text: Works joint two-stage Stage-1 delay-fit. Fitted params land fit$parList$custom_delay_params. Internally three functions assembled priors$cdf_factory, carried downstream (reconstruct / surprise / diagnostics).
code: # Each of cdf / log_cdf / log_survival is `function(theta) -> function(d)`. # Only `cdf` is required; log_cdf defaults to log(cdf), log_survival to log(1-cdf). # Supply log_survival explicitly for heavy tails (default log(1-cdf) loses precision as F->1). weibull_cdf      <- function(theta) { shape <- exp(theta[1]); scale <- exp(theta[2])  # log scale => unconstrained                                       function(d) 1 - exp(-(d/scale)^shape) } weibull_log_surv <- function(theta) { shape <- exp(theta[1]); scale <- exp(theta[2])                                       function(d) -(d/scale)^shape }            # exact, stable in the tail dly <- custom_delay(   cdf          = weibull_cdf,   log_survival = weibull_log_surv,   priors       = list(normal_prior(0,1), normal_prior(log(7),1)),  # per-param: prior=free, number=fixed   name = "Weibull", param_names = c("log_shape","log_scale"), inits = c(0, log(7)) ) # No n_params argument: it is inferred from priors / param_names / inits (must agree). validate_custom_delay(dly)             # REQUIRES library(RTMB) model(nb_likelihood(), ar1_epidemic(), dly)

code: # Builds a candidate grid (epidemic process x delay) sized to the series length, # backtests + scores it, refits the winner. Returns a nowcast_class with the # scoreboard in @comparison = list(scores, chosen, metric, max_time). nc <- auto_nowcast(   data,                          # tbl_now   metric = "wis",                # "wis"|"ape"|"mse"|"coverage_50"(|cov50-.5|)|"coverage_90"(|cov90-.9|)|"coverage"(both)   type   = "auto",               # backtest + final fit strategy   sir = NULL, ar = NULL, hsgp = NULL,   # pass a component to inject priors + force it in   delays = NULL,                 # default {lognormal, gen-gamma, dirichlet}   likelihood = nb_likelihood(),  # single, OR list(nb_likelihood(), poisson_likelihood())   models = NULL,                 # extra model() objects (e.g. custom_delay/custom_epidemic) to compare   n_dates = 6, n_draws_select = 500,    # fast selection backtest   n_draws = 2000, K = 25,        # full final refit   min_ar = 15, min_hsgp = 30)    # length thresholds # Epidemic candidates by max_time: <min_ar -> {SIR}; [min_ar,min_hsgp) -> {SIR,AR1}; # >=min_hsgp -> {AR1,HSGP}. Any explicit sir=/ar=/hsgp= is force-included. # Set future::plan(multisession) before calling for parallel backtesting.  # Accessors (prefer over reaching into @comparison): best_model_name(nc)    # winning label, e.g. "SIR/nb/Dirichlet" (= @comparison$chosen) best_model(nc)         # the winning model() object (= nc@model), reusable in nowcast()/backtest() comparison_scores(nc)  # the ranked scoreboard data.frame (= @comparison$scores) best_score(nc)         # the single scoreboard row for the winner selection_metric(nc)   # the metric used (= @comparison$metric) # best_model_name/comparison_scores/best_score/selection_metric error on a plain # nowcast() (no @comparison); best_model() works on any nowcast. print(nc) shows # the top of the scoreboard when @comparison is present.

title: Custom Delays and Epidemic Processes
text: code matters. discrete-time SIR susceptibles (S) infectious () evolving daily basis. modelled incidence new infections beta·S·/N. parameters (R0, gamma, I0) log scale (unconstrained). Wrap custom_epidemic() (argument shape custom_delay()):
code: sir_intensity_fn <- function(theta) {   #Assigning in a for loop a vector requires this:   `[<-`     <- RTMB::ADoverload("[<-")               #We define R0, gamma and I0 as the parameters we are adjusting:   R0        <- exp(theta[1])   #Basic reproductive number   gamma     <- exp(theta[2])   #1 / infectious rate   I0        <- exp(theta[3])   #Initial infected      #The total size of the population is constant:   N         <- 1e5      #Initial values for S and I   S         <- N - I0   I         <- I0      #Beta (for force of infection)   beta      <- R0 * gamma / N      #Empty vector where we'll store the incidence. Has to be instantiated in RTMB   incidence <- numeric(max_time)    #Only loops that don't depend on parameters are allowed.   #Here we loop through a constant (time) which is valid   for (t in seq_len(max_time)) {      new_inf      <-  beta * S * I     incidence[t] <- new_inf      #Rest of the model     S <- S - new_inf     I <- I + new_inf - gamma * I   }   # log of pmax(incidence, 0), AD-safe, guarding log(0):   matrix(log((incidence + abs(incidence)) * 0.5 + 1e-8), max_time, 1L) } custom_sir_epidemic <- custom_epidemic(   intensity_fn = sir_intensity_fn,   priors       = list(normal_prior(log(1.5), 0.4),   # log R0                       normal_prior(log(0.1), 0.3),   # log gamma                       normal_prior(log(5),   1.0)),  # log I0   name         = "SIR",   param_names  = c("log_R0", "log_gamma", "log_I0"),   inits        = c(log(1.5), log(0.1), log(5)) ) validate_custom_epidemic(custom_sir_epidemic)

what: 4. Advanced: A differential equations epidemic process
title: Custom Delays and Epidemic Processes
text: write epidemic continuous-time SIR ordinary differential equation let proper solver integrate . RTMBode package provides deSolve-style ode() differentiable RTMB (supplies adjoint), need hand-roll integrator Runge–Kutta. SIR system \frac{dS}{dt} = -\beta\,S\,, \qquad \frac{dI}{dt} = \beta\,S\,- \gamma\,, \qquad \beta = \frac{R_0\,\gamma}{N}, daily incidence number new infections within day. obtain adding cumulative-infection compartment C dC/dt = \beta\,S\,; per-day incidence diff(C) across day boundaries 0, 1, \dots, \texttt{max\_time}. RTMBode optional dependency; install kaskr r-universe: wrapping fitting exactly :
code: install.packages("RTMBode", repos = "https://kaskr.r-universe.dev") sir_ode_fn <- function(theta) {   #We define R0, gamma and I0 as the parameters we are adjusting (log scale,   #so they are always positive):   R0    <- exp(theta[1])   #Basic reproductive number   gamma <- exp(theta[2])   #Recovery rate (1 / infectious period)   I0    <- exp(theta[3])   #Initial infected    #The total population is constant; beta is the transmission rate:   N     <- 1e5   beta  <- R0 * gamma / N    #The SIR right-hand side, deSolve-style: a function of (time, state, parms)   #returning the derivatives. We add a compartment C that ACCUMULATES new   #infections, so the daily incidence is simply diff(C).   sir_rhs <- function(time, state, parms) {     with(as.list(c(state, parms)), {       infection <- beta * S * I       list(c(-infection,                # dS/dt               infection - gamma * I,    # dI/dt               infection))               # dC/dt  (cumulative infections)     })   }    #RTMBode::ode is a deSolve-compatible solver that is differentiable through   #RTMB (it supplies the adjoint), so we let it integrate the system instead of   #hand-rolling RK4. Solve at the day boundaries 0, 1, ..., max_time:   solution  <- RTMBode::ode(     y     = c(S = N - I0, I = I0, C = 0),     times = seq.int(0L, max_time),     func  = sir_rhs,     parms = c(beta = beta, gamma = gamma)   )   incidence <- diff(solution[, "C"])     # new infections within each day    # log of pmax(incidence, 0), AD-safe, guarding log(0):   matrix(log((incidence + abs(incidence)) * 0.5 + 1e-8), max_time, 1L) } sir_ode_epidemic <- custom_epidemic(   intensity_fn = sir_ode_fn,   priors       = list(normal_prior(log(1.5), 0.4),                       normal_prior(log(0.1), 0.3),                       normal_prior(log(5),   1.0)),   name         = "SIR-ODE",   param_names  = c("log_R0", "log_gamma", "log_I0"),   inits        = c(log(1.5), log(0.1), log(5)) )  #Check the custom model validate_custom_epidemic(sir_ode_epidemic)  #Do the nowcast nc_ode <- nowcast(mpox_tn,                   model(nb_likelihood(), sir_ode_epidemic, lognormal_delay()),                   temporal_effects = "none")  nowcast_diagnostic(nc_ode)

title: diseasenowcasting — Bayesian Epidemic Nowcasting
text: Surveillance systems delay true date event (event_date, e.g. symptom onset testing) report date event (report_date, e.g. case entered database). recent event-dates still missing reports yet arrived, latest case counts look artificially low. nowcast corrects reporting delay estimates eventual, fully-observed totals. diseasenowcasting fits censored Bayesian models. reporting delay modeled directly stochastic process, jointly epidemic dynamics, censored likelihood. Inference runs R’s Template Model Builder (RTMB), Stan/JAGS compilation required. package supports several epidemic processes, several delay families, stratified data, extreme value detection backtesting. ⚠️ diseasenowcasting currently active development parts interface might still change.

code: data(flusight, package = "tbl.now")  # Cumulative influenza hospitalisations for California, re-reported week by week california <- flusight |>   filter(location_name == "California", target_end_date >= as.Date("2023-10-01"))  flu_tbl <- tbl_now(   california,   event_date  = target_end_date,  # the epiweek being counted   report_date = as_of,            # when that cumulative count was known   case_count  = observation,      # cumulative admissions (can revise up OR down)   data_type   = "count-cumulative",   now         = as.Date("2024-01-27") )  flu_model <- model(   likelihood   = nb_likelihood(),   epidemic     = ar1_epidemic(),   delay        = lognormal_delay(),   cumulative = cumulative_process()   # <- models the up- and down-revisions )  flu_ncast <- nowcast(flu_tbl, flu_model, n_draws = 1000) autoplot(flu_ncast)

text: data tbl_now object (tbl.now::tbl_now()). metric Selection criterion. "wis" (default, lowest Weighted Interval Score), "ape" (lowest absolute percentage error median), "mse" (lowest mean squared error), one calibration criteria, pick model whose empirical interval coverage closest nominal: "coverage_50" (smallest |0.50 - coverage_50|), "coverage_90" (smallest |0.90 - coverage_90|), "coverage" (smallest |0.50 - coverage_50| + |0.90 - coverage_90|, .e. intervals jointly). type Stage strategy used backtest final fit: "auto" (default), "two_stage", "one_stage" (see nowcast()). sir, ar, hsgp Optional epidemic-process components (e.g. sir_epidemic(R0 = ...)) carrying priors.  supplied, process forced candidate grid; otherwise plain constructor used series length calls . delays list delay components compare.  Default: list(lognormal_delay(), generalized_gamma_delay(), dirichlet_delay()). likelihood Either single likelihood used every candidate (default nb_likelihood()), list likelihoods compare , e.g. list(nb_likelihood(), poisson_likelihood()). models Optional model() object list (e.g. carrying custom_delay() / custom_epidemic()) appended candidate grid compete backtest. n_dates Number historical dates backtest (default 6). n_draws_select Posterior draws selection backtest (default 500 – kept small speed). n_draws Posterior draws final fit winning model (default 2000). K_select Delay imputations selection backtest (default 10 – kept small speed, like n_draws_select).  selection backtest fits whole grid many dates, cost scales K_select; ranking candidates robust coarser imputation final fit. code: # Pure random walk on log-incidence (max_time = 20) # Uses cumsum() — no [<- assignment needed, so fully AD-safe. max_time <- 20L rw_fn <- function(theta) {   log_mu0  <- theta[1]   sigma_rw <- exp(theta[2])   eps      <- theta[3:(2L + max_time)]   lm       <- log_mu0 + cumsum(sigma_rw * eps)   matrix(lm, max_time, 1L) } # n_params is inferred (here 2 + max_time) from the priors list: custom_epi <- custom_epidemic(   rw_fn,   priors   = c(list(normal_prior(2, 1), normal_prior(-2, 0.5)),                rep(list(std_normal_prior()), max_time)),   name     = "RandomWalk",   param_names = c("log_mu0", "log_sigma", paste0("eps_", seq_len(max_time))),   inits    = c(2, -2, rep(0, max_time)) )

title: Validate a custom delay distribution for RTMB traceability — validate_custom_delay
code: # Custom components tape USER functions, so RTMB must be attached # (it is kept in Imports, not Depends, so attach it yourself): library(RTMB) weibull_cdf <- function(theta) {   shape <- exp(theta[1]); scale <- exp(theta[2])   function(d) 1 - exp(-(d / scale)^shape) } dly <- custom_delay(weibull_cdf,                     priors = list(normal_prior(0, 1), normal_prior(log(7), 1)),                     name = "Weibull", inits = c(0, log(7))) validate_custom_delay(dly) #> ✔ Custom delay `Weibull` passes RTMB traceability check.

code: # Custom components tape USER functions, so RTMB must be attached # (it is kept in Imports, not Depends, so attach it yourself): library(RTMB) max_time <- 15L rw_fn <- function(theta)   matrix(theta[1] + cumsum(exp(theta[2]) * theta[3:(2L + max_time)]), max_time, 1L) custom_epi <- custom_epidemic(   rw_fn,   priors = c(list(normal_prior(2, 1), normal_prior(-2, 0.5)),              rep(list(std_normal_prior()), max_time)),   inits  = c(2, -2, rep(0, max_time)) ) validate_custom_epidemic(custom_epi) #> ✔ Custom epidemic `Custom` passes RTMB traceability check.
